title: Cities Face Difficulties Canceling Flock Contracts
excerpt: Several cities are encountering challenges and ignored requests when attempting to terminate their contracts with Flock Safety.
body_html:
A growing number of cities are attempting to cancel their agreements with Flock Safety, only to encounter significant obstacles during the process. According to reports, some municipalities are finding it surprisingly difficult to end their business relationships with the company.

For example, the city council in Plymouth, Minnesota, voted to end its contract with Flock in September. However, the company reportedly failed to respond to the city's cancellation request. Because of the lack of response, the surveillance cameras remained installed for over a month after the termination vote.

As more local governments reassess their use of these automated license plate reading systems, the complications surrounding contract exits and hardware removal continue to draw attention.
